Definition: from G4190; depravity, i.e. (specially), malice; plural (concretely) plots, sins:--iniquity, wickedness.
BiblicalUsage: Poneria is depravity, wickedness worked out in deeds. Jesus sees through the Pharisees and names their wickedness to their faces, and Paul warns of spiritual wickedness in high places. Luke shows it closer to home, in hearts full of ravening, and Romans lists it among the sins that fill a godless mind.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe wickedness is not only what people do in the dark, but a power that works in high places and in ordinary hearts alike. That is why the gospel answers it with armour, not with better intentions.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
